encoder: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), a single agent working alone from the brief in BRIEF.md, with no subagents
display_name: Interpretation Act 2005 (Ireland): executable time, commencement, construction and repeal rules, refusing where the Act is silent

l4_build.note: check.sh was run with L4_TARGET=unstable (the default in this row's check.sh); the brief requires @lang en, REFUSE and YMD, which main rejects, so no main comparison was made.

source.kind: unofficial plain-text rendering of the English enacted text; not the official text

scope.encoded: s 1(2); s 2(1) and (2); s 3(1) and (2); s 4; ss 5 to 9; s 11 to s 13; s 14(1); s 15(1); s 16; s 17; s 18(b), (d), (e), (f), (g), (h), (i) as a named refusal; s 20(1); s 21(2); s 22(3); s 25; s 26; s 27; the Schedule's time words (commencement, financial year, local financial year, midnight, month, week, week-day, year), 'full age', 'working day' and 'public holiday' (as an input).
scope.inert: s 1(1); s 10; s 14(2) and (3); s 15(2); s 18(a), (c), (j); s 19; s 20(2); s 22(1) and (2); s 23; s 24; the long title; the lexical entries of Schedule Parts 1 and 2 (reasons in NOTES.md section 4).
scope.not_encoded: a calendar of holidays (an input); clock times under the Standard Time (Amendment) Act 1971; how a person attains an age (inputs); the Irish-language text.
scope.refuses: where the Act has no rule: a period of months or years that does not begin on the first day of the unit; a period of weeks that does not begin on a Sunday; any period counted after an event; a last day that falls on a day of rest, recess or holiday; the moment of commencement under s 16(1); a Saorstat Eireann statute silent on commencement; a time expressed by hour; a time of service once the contrary is proved.
scope.readings_not_the_acts: ie-month-year-readings.l4 holds the alternative readings (clamped corresponding date, first day included, rolled corresponding date, seven-day week, roll-forward off a rest day); the Act's own modules never call it.

not_reviewed: No domain expert has read this encoding against the statute. It was written by one agent from the unofficial plain-text rendering and checked only by its own tests, the self-check in check.sh and the quotation gate; no second reader has compared it with the official text of the Act, and the Irish-language text was not consulted.
